body.p: Nelge-Kokora. There were three brothers. The elder brother's wife ran [away] forever. The elder brother had the name Nelge-Kokora. The elder brother was suffering, he suffered a lot. So he suffered for one year. Then he went to search his wife. The elder brother went for a long time, he went everywhere. He made a lot of paths, he didn't find his wife. Then the elder brother saw an old man on the way. The old man said to the elder brother: "Where are you going, man?" There the elder brother said: "My wife went away forever. Where she had gone, I don't know. I'm missing my wife. I am suffering! Oh, old man, help me! Say a good word to me! Offer me good advise! Where will I go? Along which way will I go? Where will I find my wife?" The old man listened, having listened he said to Nelge-Kokora: "You go to the forest! There you see a horse! Tie the horse to a tree! And you yourself turn into a hare! When you turn into a hare, then search the Upper World! Then lie down with the ear on the earth and listen!" So the old man said. Nelge-Kokora went off. On the third day he came to forest. Here he is sitting, he sat all the night. On the fourth day early in the morning Nelge-Kokora saw the horse. He caught the horse, having caught he tied it to a tree, he tied up the horse firmly. Then he himself turned into a hare, he ran, he ran quickly. The hare reached the Upper World. Having arrived he lay down on the earth, then he is listening. Now the hare hears: [someone] is singing, dancing, and is playing and laughing, they are celebrating a wedding. The hare is surprised: "What devils are celebrating a wedding"? Then he ran, he was running and running, he found one tent. In this tent there was a devil, the Baba Yaga. The Baba Yaga devil was like this: one eye, one tooth, one leg. The hare jumped quickly into the tent. The Baba Yaga devil saw the hare and went off. Then the hare shapeshifted again, [it is] again a human. Here Nelhe-Kokora saw many people. One old man says: "Where are you going, man? What are you looking for? Have you come for the wedding?" Nelhe-Kokora said: "What kind of wedding was it?" The old man says: "It was your wife's wedding!" There Nelhe-Kokora asks the old man: "Eh, old man! Tell me one word, who, what kind of human has stolen my wife? Tell me one word, who is the thief?" The old man said: "Take the direct way, there you'll find!" Nelhe-Kokora turned into a hare again and ran along the direct way. He was running and running, he was running for three days. On the fourth day he found a tent. In this tent the thief is sitting.[DCh]: Not clear why dative-locative case at direct object. The hare ran around the tent, then he jumped on one foot into the tent. Having jumped [inside] he saw [DCh]: The form "minin" is his(?) wife, the woman was sitting and silently crying. The hare says to the thief: "What kind of awkward and the analysis is tentative.wedding did you have? There was very little meat. They were eating poorly (?). My(?) wife is suffering. What kind of wedding is this?!" The thief got very angry, he says so: "Oh, hare, don't speak badly! What do you need? I have apparently a lot of food. [If] you want, eat! Don't speak badly!" The hare also says: "What a good human you are! What a rich human! What good words! When your wife gives birth to a child for you, then I'll eat your food!" The thief got very angry again. "Don't talk badly", the thief says, "I'll kill you! Don't talk!" Then the hare says: "Eh, thief, please don't kill [me]!" The thief says: "What kind of name is "thief"? Do you know?" "I know", the hare says. "Ha, ha, ha", the thief is laughing. "Ha, ha, ha", he says. "What do you know, cross-eyed?! You don't see straightly!" "Cross-eyed", he [= the thief(?)] says, "do I know?!" "[You're] a fool, a fraidy cat!" The hare turned again into a human, then he got very angry, he says: "You're the thief! You stole my wife", so Nelhe-Kokora says. Having said this he took the horse's head, he darted the head to the thief. The horse's head flew past [the thief], it killed forty people. Now the thief says: "Eh, [DCh]: The analysis of man, please don't kill [me]! You've killed forty people, that's bad!"bajÉÉ£miÅ¡" is obscure and tentative. You've killed forty people in vain! Please don't kill [me]! Don't get angry![DCh]: The form Be good, man!" Nelhe-Kokora got angry again, and he darted a knife to the thief."tikulidi" seems to be incomplete. The thief dodged, the knife killed thirty people. The thief is begging Nelhe-Kokora again. Nelhe-Kokora said: "Don't talk! I'll kill you! I'll take my wife. [If] you want, let's divide fairly!" "Well, let's run to the upper World. Let's fight there! [If] you kill me, it's your wife; [if] I kill you, it's my wife! Do you want it like that?" "Fine, let's run!" "Let's run", the thief said. Then Nelhe-Kokora and the thief were running. Nelhe-Kokora first ran to the upper world, once he hit the thief and killed him. Having killed [him], Nelhe-Kokora turned again into a hare and ran back to the tent. He was running and running, he reached the tent. Here the hare again turned into a human, then he took his wife, he brought [her] back to the older brothers' tent. He reached the tent. He came there and made a new tent. There he lived, the rich Nelhe-Kokora is living. The father said to the children: "I'll go and have a look what kind of woman Nelhe-Kokora has brought?" The old man went into Nelhe-Kokora's tent. He came [in] and he says: "My child, show me the daughter-in-law!" Nelhe-Kokora says: "Look!" The old man looked, having looked he says: "Your [DCh]: The form "hiÉ£uni" is unclear.wife is more beautiful than the sun!" Then he went off to his own tent.[DCh]: Not clear why POSS2SG at the emphatic pronoun. The father said to the children: "My daughter-in-law is very beautiful, better than the sun!" The younger brother listened, having listened the younger brother said: "I'll go to my older brother and have a look at my sister-in-law!" "Well, go", the father says. The younger brother went to Nelhe-Kokora's tent. He came there. The elder brother is not in the tent, only his sister-in-law is sitting there. The younger brother says: "Where is the older brother?" He himself is watching his sister-in-law. The sister-in-law says: "My husband went to hunt wild reindeers." Then the younger brother sat down in the tent, he himself is watching his sister-in-law. The younger brother thinks: "Father has told the truth, my sister-in-law is more beautiful than the sun." There the younger brother went back to his own tent. He came there.[DCh]: Not clear why POSS2SG at emphatic pronoun. The father said to the younger brother: "Did you see your sister-in-law? Is she good?" The younger brother doesn' t answer. The other day the younger brother says to his father: "My brain is bursting.[DCh]: The analysis of "kaputÄu" is tentative. I am suffering! I love my sister-in-law! I'll take my sister-in-law, ok?" The father listened the younger brother, having listened he said: "That's bad!" The younger brother again begs his father: "Help me, father! My brain is bursting![DCh]: The analysis of "kaputÄu" is tentative. I am suffering! Please help me, father!" The father listened to the younger brother, having listened he said again: "That's bad!" The younger brother started to cry, he was crying and crying, he got angry, he got very angry. There the younger brother said to his father for the third time: "I won't be able to endure! I'll kill the older brother! I'll take my sister-in-law![DCh]: Not clear why plural marking here. I am suffering heavily! Please help(?) [me with] the bad! I am asking for the last [DCh]: The analysis is very tentative.time!" The father listened to the younger brother, having again listened he said: "Fine! I'll help you, my child! Let's make it so now: I am ill. You look for a shaman! You are searching a shaman, bring [him] to me! Well, go, quickly!" The younger brother went off. On the fifth day he found a tent. In this tent there was a shaman sitting.[DCh]: Not clear why dative-locative case at direct object. The younger brother said: "Where do I find the shaman?" The shaman said: "What do you need?" The younger brother says: "My father is sick, let's go to the old man! Please help my father!" The shaman said: "Well, let's go!" Then they went off. They reached [DCh]: Case the father's tent. The father said to the children: "The shaman is staying alone in the tent, you go out!"marking seems to be confused here. The children went off. Then the father says to the shaman: "I am eaten by a devil. Take away the devil! Put the devil into my daughter-in-law, she dies [then]! Make it like that! So it has to be!" The shaman listened to the old man, having listened he went to the older brother's tent.[DCh]: Not clear why plural marking here; the story is only about one older brother. The older brother is not in the tent. Only the daughter-in-law is sitting. The shaman watched the daughter-in-law. The daughter-in-law smiled. "Where is the man?", the shaman says. The daughter-in-law said: "My husband went to hunt wild reindeers!" Then the daughter-in-law is laughing again. The shaman says: "What are you laughing?" "[Just] so", the daughter-in-law said. Then the daughter-in-law was about to feed the shaman. "Sit down, old man, sit down", the daughter-in-law says, "eat! Do you like the meat of wild reindeers? Eat, old man", so the daughter-in-law fed the shaman. The shaman is eating and thinks for himself: "What a good woman she is, better than the sun!" Having eaten the shaman went to the father's tent. The father said: "Did you see the daughter-in-law?" The shaman says: "I have seen [her]. I won't kill your daughter-in- law! I feel sorry for the daughter-in-law!" So the shaman said, and he went to his own tent. The father got angry. "What kind of shaman is he? [Such a] dog!" The shaman went away forever. The father is worrying: "How do I kill my daughter-in-law? It will be bad", so the father is worrying. The younger brother came. The younger brother again says to the father: "Oh, father, it's difficult for me! I'll take my sister-in-law! I'll kill my older brother! I am suffering!" The old man listened, having listened he said: "Which shaman is better? Go tomorrow and search the Baba Yaga shaman! Bring the Baba Yaga here!" Early in the morning the younger brother went off. On the third day he found a tent. In this tent the Baba Yaga is sitting. The younger brother came silently there. The Baba Yaga is sneezing, she sneezed three times. Then the Baba Yaga said: "What kind of person is coming? Which one is coming? Whose one?" The younger brother said: "A human has come. My father is sick, help! Do something good, please!" The Baba Yaga said: "Who is your father? Who will I go to?" The younger brother said: "My father is Bambaj!" "Well, let's go", the Baba Yaga says. On the second day they(?) came to the father's tent. The father said: "I am sick. You take the devil [away]! Put this devil into the daughter-in-law! Kill the daughter-in-law! So it has to be!" The Baba Yaga listened. Having listened she went to the older [DCh]: Not clear from the context why brother's tent. The daughter-in-law is sitting alone in the tent. The Baba Yaga watched the daughter-in-law.plural marking here. The Baba Yaga says: "Where is the man?" The daughter-in-law said: "My husband went to hunt wild reindeers." Then the daughter-in-law offered [something] to the Baba Yaga, she did well (?). The Baba Yaga won't kill the daughter-in-law. Having watched the daughter-in-law the Baba Yaga went again to the father's tent. The father said: "Did you kill the daughter-in-law?" The Baba Yaga says: "No!" There the old father got very angry. The Baba Yaga went away to her own tent forever. The father thought: "Who helps me? How will I kill my daughter-in-law? Who, whom will I call?" So it was, the father was always thinking. The younger brother is asking the father again: "Oh, father! I'll take my sister-in-law! I'll kill my older brother! It's torturous for me! I am sick", so the younger brother says for the third time. The father listened again, he listened for the third time. Having listened he said: "Bad! My beloved child, go! Search the wolf shaman! Bring the wolf shaman to me!" The younger brother went off again. He was searching and searching the wolf shaman, then he found [him]. Having found the wolf shaman he grabbed him at his tail and carried him to the father. The shaman wolf got very angry. The father was afraid. There the father said: "Eh, children, bring the wolf back!" The children brought the wolf shaman back. The father thought again: "How will I kill my daughter-in-law? I asked all upper shamans, they won't kill, didn't help." Then the father called the older and the younger brother, and there he said: "I am very sick! Bring me a shaman of the Lower World!" The daughter-in-law says to her husband: "The father sends you to the Lower World, don't go, you will die!" The older brother says: "How will I not go? The father is sending [me]! He is sick!" The wife listened, having listened the thought. Then she said: "Fine! Go! When you go, take forty decks of cards. Play cards! [If] it's bad, then show this letter of mine!" The man took forty decks of cards and the letter, then he went into the earth. The older brother fell into the Lower World. Here in the Lower World the older brother saw people [from the] Lower World. The people from the Lower World don't see the older brother. The people from the Lower World say: "Why does the fire crackle?" The older brother sat down close to a girl. The girl got sick at once. The people from the Lower World are surprised, why did the girl fall ill? It becomes night. The human from the Upper World lay down with the girl. In the morning the girl was very sick. Then the people from the Lower World called the middle shaman. That shaman didn't help. Then they called the big shaman. This shaman saw the human from the Upper World. Having seen he said: "How are you here? What do you need?" The older brother says: "Let's play cards!" Then the big shaman and the older brother are playing cards. They used(?) forty decks of cards, the human from the Upper World didn't win. Then the older brother showed the big shaman his letter. The big shaman read the letter and so was the letter: "Lower Shaman, big one! I am asking you, big shaman! Eat the father and my husband's younger brother!" The big shaman said: "Fine! Catch a white horse! Cut off the horse's tongue! Forge an iron tongue! Put this iron tongue into the horse's mouth!" The people from the Lower World are doing so. They caught a white horse. They cut off the horse's tongue. Then they forged an iron tongue. They put the iron tongue into the horse's mouth. On that horse the big shaman and the human from the Upper World went to the Upper World. They were going and going, they found a hole. The big shaman shouted: "Gek!" There he jumped off (?). Having jumped off he dragged the human from the Upper World. Then they went to the father's tent. They came there. Then the father and the younger brother was brought by the big shaman to the Lower World. The hole was closed by the white horse.
